text:
alex: Heads-up — ran nsys on the prod-like workload after the runtime change and seeing a kernel-selection regression. MatMul falls back to the native algo much more often; timeline shows more and longer kernel spans + host stalls. Perfetto & nsys captures attached (links). Anyone else seeing this?

maya: Ugh. Can you paste the timeline excerpt or a short nsys snippet? Did we change selector heuristics recently? @sanjay did you land anything?

alex: Here’s the short excerpt from the after-run nsys timeline I clipped:
```
# nsys timeline excerpt (after commit)
[GPU] 0.000s - 0.002s : kernel launch overhead
[GPU] 0.002s - 0.013s : matmul_quantized_algoA   (duration 11.2ms)
[GPU] 0.013s - 0.040s : matmul_native_algoB      (duration 27.0ms)
[GPU] 0.041s - 0.050s : postprocess kernels
# KV-cache events (timestamps): eviction spike @0.012s, 0.028s
```
Before traces used algoA almost continuously for the same step. After trace shows interleaving and an extra big native kernel.

maya: That native kernel is ~2-3x slower in the trace. We should compare the same exact input (seq_len/batch) before/after. Any git commit candidate?

sanjay: I did rebase & tweak the selection thresholds last week. I changed the fallback multiplier from 1.2 -> 1.05 to reduce wrong-picks for long sequences. Could have made selector too eager to pick safe/native kernel. I can repro locally.

dora: CI bisect kicked off on the perf baseline; pointing at a small change. @ci-bot any update?

ci-bot: git bisect complete: first-bad is 8b7a3c (kernel-selector: adjust fallback cost threshold), good is 8b6f2a.

alex: Nice — that lines up. I ran microbenchmarks on both commits:
```
# microbench results (matmul key kernel)
commit 8b6f2a (before): avg 9.1 ms, p95 11.4 ms
commit 8b7a3c (after) : avg 25.2 ms, p95 31.7 ms
end-to-end p95 latency delta ~+18% on our small-slab workload
```

maya: Two angles: revert the threshold change or make it adaptive to input characteristics (seq_len, batch). Also the KV-cache eviction spikes at the same times make me wonder if selector change touches buffer allocations or causes extra memcpy which shifts alignment.

sanjay: Good catch — my change added a safety memcpy path when estimating memory headroom (to be conservative). That memcpy is small but could nudge allocation offsets. I'll instrument the runtime to log allocation alignment + memcpy counts per request.

alex: Please also capture perfetto comparisons (we need full GPU kernel timeline and host stacks). Attach nsys .nsys and perfetto links in the PR. For the rollback plan: canary revert in Dedicated for 24h while we test patch.

dora: I'll open a short-lived rollback PR and schedule canary. Put clear metrics: kernel-selection ratio for algoA vs native, matmul avg time, KV eviction rate.

maya: For the fix, instead of a flat multiplier change maybe we use a sigmoid on estimated perf ratio that depends on seq_len. That avoids flipping to native for borderline cases. Also add a regression test that simulates our slab allocations so memcpy/alignments are exercised.

sanjay: Will prototype. Quick local commands I used to reproduce:
```
# reproducible profiling steps
# checkout before
git checkout 8b6f2a && \
nsys profile -o before.nsys --trace=nvtx,cuda python run_infer.py --seq 2048 --batch 8 --steps 50
# checkout after
git checkout 8b7a3c && \
nsys profile -o after.nsys --trace=nvtx,cuda python run_infer.py --seq 2048 --batch 8 --steps 50
# perf summary (quick):
nvprof --print-gpu-trace before.nsys | grep matmul | awk '{print $3,$5}'
```

alex: Thanks. Once you have the patch, add the before/after nsys captures to the PR and include a tiny perfetto trace diff screenshot in the description. We'll keep the canary until p95 is back in line. :thumbsup:

dora: I'll coordinate the canary and set dashboards to alert if matmul native ratio >10% or p95 regresses >5%.

alex: One more note — KV-cache logs show eviction-burst correlation with the slow native kernel. If we can suppress the extra memcpy or avoid moving slab offsets, eviction spikes disappear in my local trace. Prioritize that path.

maya: Great. Ping here when you have the patched branch and the nsys/perfetto artifacts.

(small reactions :thumbsup: from the channel)
